newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-SPINNERS COULD DECIDE FIRST TEST, SAYS HOUGHTON.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SPINNERS COULD DECIDE FIRST TEST, SAYS HOUGHTON.

text.p: Dave Houghton, player-coach of Zimbabwe's buoyant cricketers, expects their first-ever test against England starting at Queen's Club on Wednesday to be decided by spin.

Zimbabwe lifted their confidence for the ground-breaking match when they beat England by two wickets in the first one-day international on Sunday, a game that convinced Houghton the slow bowlers could play crucial roles in the test.

Former Zimbabwe captain Houghton said: "I think the test pitch will have a bit more bounce and carry than the one we used on Sunday, but the way it dusted up after just 100 overs makes me think the spinners might have a big say in the test.
"(Leg-spinner) Paul Strang will be our potential matchwinner and we'll rely on Grant Flower as the second spinner."
Houghton believes the pitch will not last five days, saying: "I think the match will be all over in four days and I just hope that we're on the right side of the result."

If Houghton is right, England will need off-spinner Robert Croft and left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell in prime form. Croft bowled well against Matabeleland in the four-day game last week but Tufnell was disappointing.

England are struggling to shake off the wretched form that has marked most of their tour performances, though has Atherton played down the significance of Sunday's defeat, their third in six tour matches.

Houghton, keen to have the efforts of Zimbabwe's bowlers acknowledged, said: "England have been here long enough now to have adjusted to the conditions and their batsmen should be coming into form. But I don't think they give enough credit to our bowlers when they talk about why they hve failed to make big scores.

"We are playing the best cricket we have played for many years now and if we can keep this squad together I think the results will begin to show. I agree that we are a well equipped one-day side, but I actually think that we are an even better test side".

England's selection options are limited. Their squad, cut to 14 after paceman Dominic Cork pulled out just before the party left so he could resolve personal problems, has been further hit by injury to all-rounder Ronnie Irani.
Irani has been sent to a hospital in Harare for a bone scan on his injured back and is probably out of contention.

With wicketkeeper Jack Russell likely to be left out so England can play six specialist batsman -- Alec Stewart would keep wicket -- the final place appears to be between pace bowlers Andy Caddick and Chris Silverwood.

Caddick can pose awkward problems with his height and movement but has not so far been at his best. Silverwood bowled with great heart and vigour on his England debut on Sunday, taking two for 27 in his 10 overs, and may have done enough to win a first test cap.

It is four years since Zimbabwe gained test status, yet their inaugural test against England was deemed so unimportant that not one high-ranking Test and County Cricket Board (TCCB) official will be at the occasion.
